sections.COMMENTS:
This Individual Source is part of the system of blind faults confined at the footwall of the Acquasanta thrust, earlier activated by the northernmost reaches of the L'Aquila 2009 sequence, and then activated in January 2017 by the 2016-2017 central Italy sequence (Bigi et al., 2013; Tondi et al., 2020; Buttinelli et al., 2021).
The 2016-17 sequence initiated during the summer of 2016 and includes a succession of moderate to strong extensional earthquakes. These events activated a ca. 70 km long, NNW-SSE trending, multiple fault systems, exhibiting complex ruptures along the backbone of the central Apennines. These events have notoriously and vastly affected the towns of Amatrice, Visso, and Norcia.
On January 2017 the 2016-2017 sequence stretched to the south, with a peak of seismic moment release occurring on 18 January within an hour time span. In particular, three shocks were stronger than Mw 5.0, the strongest one (Mw 5.5) having occurred at 10:14:09 UTC (ISIDe Working Group, 2007; Chiaraluce et al., 2017).
The 2016-2017 sequence struck a portion of the Central Apennines that was believed to be especially well known from a seismotectonic point of view. The region is undergoing SW-NE active extension; normal faulting focal mechanisms computed for the largest shocks agree with the tectonic regime of the region (Chiaraluce et al., 2017).
This SW-dipping Individual Source is part of a fault system formed during the Mesozoic and reactivated during the Miocene flexure of the foreland in response to the orogenic build-up (e.g., Tondi et al., 2020). Some of the faults formed in the previous tectonic regime were transported onto the Acquasanta thrust hanging-wall (i.e., the Monti della Laga - Gorzano fault, MLG), whereas their roots remained confined at the thrust footwall.
The inversion of strong-motion, GPS and InSAR data provides average slip and cumulative geodetic moment for the rupture (Cheloni et al., 2019).
The interpretation of seismic reflection profiles in the area (Di Bucci et al., 2021; www.retrace3d.it) allowed to image the geometry of the whole Acquasanta thrust (Buttinelli et al., 2021), dipping toward W-NW. This evidence has shown that the southern segment of the MLG in the Campotosto Lake area is detached at shallow levels, thus indicating that seismicity like that due to the 18 January 2017 earthquakes has occurred below the Acquasanta thrust (Bigi et al., 2013; Buttinelli et al., 2021).
